cards.note: no primitives icon imports anywhere: the card's *16 names in src/client/icons.tsx are local vendored components, and the only @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-primitives import is the non-icon SettingsFormModel/spec types
the plugin never reads workspace file content through the workspaceFiles Remote; its file access is the host fs SDK plus its own GitHub fetch layer

host registers no settings namespace: every card field is a volatile field on the plugin's own profile entry Config (ctx.settings.mutate/describe, configure({auto:false}) for the self-owned page); the browser card and slash dots read ctx.configForms.get('skill-hub'); the one-time legacy settings.yaml section and sidecar config are adopted at startup
the plugin ships no agent presets: its bundle patch inserts one plugin row and dsh.bundle declares no preset source

the stats reader never parses raw session logs: reads go through sessionQuery and the sessionPersistence seam whose list()/open()/read() shapes were re-checked unchanged at 0.1.7 (the V4 log stays the host's implementation detail), and event matching is by type only
the plugin configures no model provider: neither its bundle patch nor its package manifest touches the official DeepSeek adapter or any llm row

every configurable field is declared .volatile() so a settings edit commits into the running instance via loader/volatile-update (no reload); dsh.bundle.patch stays a single file because the 12-line patch needs no ordered split, which the 0.1.7 contract still accepts

informational only: the host half activates from its profile row and the browser half registers both slots with a log-never-throw failure policy, so the Plugin Manager roster and Settings stay the visibility path after a host upgrade

optional capability adopted (no workaround replaced): locale meta.title/meta.description exported at ./locale/*.json and a top-level package icon, so the Plugins manager renders the plugin's own localized card instead of the package description
the plugin stores no attachments and writes no custom session events: it only reads user/message and tool/call events that the host delivers
the plugin registers a settings.section page and a plugins.bundle.config card; it does not extend the sidebar launcher seat (settings.launcher) or the Models credential flow (settings.models.sign-in)
